title: The Parthenon Sculptures: the Trustees’ statement
author: Trustees of the British Museum

notes.text: Reviewed for A Short History of Taking Things and Keeping Them. Relevant locators: The position of the Trustees of the British Museum; Common misconceptions, especially the section concerning a Greek loan request. The statement makes recognition of the Museum's ownership a condition for considering a loan and argues that divided display has public benefit. It describes Greece as requesting permanent return, not a loan. It explicitly denies arguing that Greek institutions cannot care for the sculptures; do not attribute that argument to this statement. The legal and historical assertions are institutional positions, not MoSA's adjudication. No publication date is established. No object link is created because this registration concerns the statement and no individual sculpture has been reconciled. The official page was examined through web-indexed text; a directly accessible reusable facsimile has not been established. The Museum's general copyright page does not establish a licence for this whole statement.
